newsitem.title: UK: Crude tankers mainly stable, W.Africa-U.S. up.
newsitem.headline: Crude tankers mainly stable, W.Africa-U.S. up.

text.p: Dirty tanker fixtures stayed generally on an even keel on Thursday, with West Africa/U.S. Gulf trips showing some signs of firming on rising demand, broker said.
One broker said 130,000 tonners from West Africa to the U.S. had risen to W85 from W82.5, citing the Glenmaye chartered at this rate for Sun, loading on Jan 15.
However, the Aitolikos carrying 135,000 tonnes from Cabinda to USAC was said to have failed at W78.
In the Middle East, the Crown Jewel I was chartered with 257,000 tonnes for Stentex at W58 to Singapore, up from W55 previously.
"For 130,000 tonnes I have not seen one fixture," an Italian broker said, while for 80,000 tonnes he noted the Paris II had been fixed at a little changed W107.5 for a Libya-Trieste hop for Veba.
Fuel oil in Inter-U.K./Cont and the Med was softer, with 25,000 tonners down to W175 from W180. "There's masses of tonnage around," one broker said.
In the U.S./Caribbean, New York brokers said they had seen few new fixtures since the Christmas/New Year holiday period.
